skill.name: better-auth-best-practices
skill.description: Guide for configuring Better Auth server and client projects, including database adapters, sessions, plugins, environment variables, and common setup checks.
skill.summary: Helps agents implement Better Auth with practical configuration guidance and security-aware defaults.
skill.author: better-auth

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around configuration names and API references. Five findings are confirmed because the guide instructs agents to install packages, run Better Auth CLI commands, or modify Cursor MCP configuration. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious network behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to show the npm install command and wait for explicit user approval before changing dependencies.
Avoid @latest in automated instructions, or require a user-approved version before running npx commands.

remediation.issue: Database migration command in setup flow
remediation.suggestion: Require a database backup or generated diff review before running migration commands against a project database.
Require explicit opt-in before changing AI tool configuration or installing any MCP integration.

content.value_statement: Better Auth setup has many framework, database, session, and plugin choices. This skill gives focused guidance for server, client, environment, and security configuration.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes required Better Auth setup steps and environment variables.
Explains database adapter choices for direct connections and ORM adapters.
Highlights session storage, cookie cache, and rate limit configuration.
Lists server and client plugin import patterns and common plugins.
Calls out common Better Auth gotchas such as model names and plugin schema updates.
limitations: It is a documentation guide, not an executable integration script.
It does not verify Better Auth API changes without checking current docs.
It does not inspect a project unless the agent is asked to review files.
It does not replace security review for production authentication settings.

use_cases.title: Start a New Auth Setup
use_cases.description: Plan the server file, route handler, environment variables, and database adapter for a new Better Auth project.

use_cases.title: Add Login Features
use_cases.description: Choose Better Auth settings for email login, OAuth providers, verification emails, and reset flows.

use_cases.title: Review Production Settings
use_cases.description: Check session storage, secure cookies, rate limits, CSRF checks, origin checks, and plugin schema updates.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Better Auth to this TypeScript project. Identify the needed files, environment variables, database adapter, and route handler.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Better Auth session plan. Explain the best storage, cookie cache, expiration, refresh, and rate limit settings for this app.

prompt_templates.title: Add Plugins Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Better Auth plugins for this feature set. Include server plugin placement, client plugin placement, schema updates, and tests to run.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Auth
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Better Auth configuration for production readiness. Focus on secrets, origins, secure cookies, CSRF, sessions, database hooks, and migration risk.

output_examples.input: I need Better Auth with Prisma and email password login.
output_examples.output: A setup checklist covering environment variables, auth file placement, Prisma adapter selection, schema generation, and route handler setup.

output_examples.input: Review my session settings before production.
output_examples.output: A security-focused review of cookie security, session duration, secondary storage, rate limiting, CSRF checks, and origin checks.
A plugin plan with server imports, client plugin placement, schema regeneration, and feature testing steps.

best_practices: Confirm before running package installs, migrations, or MCP configuration commands.
Use environment variables for secrets and URLs unless a project needs explicit config.
Re-run schema generation after adding or changing Better Auth plugins.
anti_patterns: Disabling CSRF or origin checks without a documented production reason.
Using database table names where Better Auth expects adapter model names.
Assuming secondary storage sessions are also stored in the database by default.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance. Agents should ask before running installs, migrations, or MCP setup commands.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover client setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes client imports, client plugins, session methods, and separate client/server type use.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It flags secure cookies, CSRF checks, origin checks, rate limiting, cookie cache, and session storage choices.

faq.question: Does it replace official Better Auth docs?
faq.answer: No. It points users to current Better Auth docs for exact APIs and examples.

faq.question: Can it help with Prisma or Drizzle?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains ORM adapter usage and schema generation considerations.
